For two weeks there is no nurse available—with no replacement arranged and no clear plan. All bloods and other nurse appointments to be postpone to a future date. Shockingly, this is just one example of what has become the “new normal” at a surgery that used to be excellent.
When speaking to the reception team, one of them even said proudly that they’ve been there for less than two months and can’t be blamed for the decline. And honestly, I agree—this isn’t about the receptionists. It’s a management issue, and it feels long overdue for leadership to step up and take responsibility for the falling standards.
To illustrate the situation: three weeks ago I arrived at 1pm, and the waiting room was completely empty. Not a single patient. Yet despite this, the waiting list to speak to or see a doctor was still long. It makes absolutely no sense and raises serious concerns about how the practice is being run.
Overall, the surgery feels understaffed, disorganised, and unable to provide even the basics of timely care.
